name: TableBench
abstract: TableBench evaluates complex table question answering. This page uses Overall under the TCoT setting from the paper's main results table.
contributions: The paper compares multiple reasoning protocols; this page fixes TCoT as the primary leaderboard.
This keeps the core structured-data reasoning challenge while avoiding excessive page complexity.
method: TableBench targets complex table question answering in realistic industrial scenarios, going beyond simple lookup to cover fact checking, numerical reasoning, data analysis, and visualization.
It spans four major capability groups and 18 subfields, and is built through scenario analysis, manual annotation, and explicit task-complexity design to better match real-world demands.
The paper also introduces TableInstruct and TABLELLM to study textual, symbolic, and program-based reasoning strategies for tabular tasks.
The experiments show that both open-source and proprietary models still fall short of practical table-analysis needs, with even the strongest systems remaining noticeably behind humans.
